# Pinned import corpus

The original synthetic archives are distributed under the repository's [Apache-2.0 license](../../../LICENSE). They contain no third-party mods or assets. `manifest.json` pins their SHA-256 identities and independently authored expected Modrinth output members. ZIP timestamps and Unix file attributes are fixed.

The corpus covers Modrinth side-specific overrides, CurseForge common overrides, exact runtime selections, and traversal refusal. `journey_import` checks the hashes before invoking the ordinary executable, preserves imported documents across two syncs, and compares the complete exported content inventory and runtime metadata. The fixture expectation is not derived from empack's importer or writer.

Run `python3 scripts/check-import-corpus.py` from the repository root. It uses the shared verification runner, including executable identity and result receipts. This local corpus needs no network, Java, or provider credentials. It does not qualify external provider behavior or real launcher/game consumption.

Changes to archives or expected output require deliberate review of both the source contents and expectations. The checker never refreshes them. Moving upstream packs belong to `scripts/survey-imports.py`; survey observations cannot replace these pinned expectations.

## Pinned upstream packs

The `pinned-import` live suite uses fixed upstream archives and independently reviewed inventories. All five scenarios share acquisition, import, convergence, complete export and edit/adopt checks. Each uses its pinned version; launcher execution remains a separate consumer check. Their expectations remain separate from moving survey results.

### Fabulously Optimized 6.5.0

`fabulously-optimized-6.5.0.json` records Fabulously Optimized 6.5.0, Modrinth project `1KVo5zza`, version `N276l2ON`. The archive is 177,589 bytes. Its SHA-512 matches the version record; SHA-256 and the override inventories were computed independently with Python's ZIP reader, without empack. No upstream archive, mod, resource pack or configuration bytes are committed here.

The expectation retains all 50 declared files (44,322,932 bytes), ordered download fallbacks, hashes, sizes and side requirements, plus hashes and sizes for all 63 overrides. The source index declares every file required on both sides; project catalog labels do not override those declarations. The runtime is Minecraft 1.21.1 with Fabric loader 0.19.3. All payload members are ordinary `overrides/` files, including the opaque `resourcepacks/Mod Menu Helper.zip`; there are no optional files, auxiliary payloads or side-specific exclusions in this pack. The synthetic and controlled fixtures cover those other decisions.

Run `python3 scripts/verify.py pinned-import`. This ignored live suite downloads the exact archive into a disposable workspace, checks both archive digests before import, and uses fresh isolated state/cache paths. The first sync may materialize referenced files; the second must preserve the full author tree, including bytes, attributes and empty directories. It also checks the complete Modrinth export and all acquired bytes in a bundled Prism export. Imported overrides are locked local dependencies. After an edit, sync must refuse and preserve the prior lock/artifacts; explicit adoption accepts the changed bytes. Without a version bump, the next Modrinth export must contain that edit while preserving the earlier bundled artifact and author metadata. Only the two generated launcher metadata files may exist outside the expected game inventory. No Java or launcher is executed. Network failure fails the attempt; the test does not select a newer version or retry the whole journey.

Archive acquisition has a 60-second deadline and reads at most the declared size plus one byte. Each CLI command has a 600-second deadline. The four smaller fixtures limit each output member to 16 MiB and the bundled archive to 64 MiB decoded/255 entries; the saved-world fixture below has separate measured payload bounds. All downloaded and generated bytes are temporary; receipts retain source/test identity and outcomes rather than republishing the pack.

The pack's [pinned license](https://github.com/Fabulously-Optimized/fabulously-optimized/blob/a20d4bf2ab7f7be8741aaeca2211ef1899c6e8ed/LICENSE.md) is BSD-3-Clause, copyright Fabulously Optimized Authors. Referenced mods retain their own licenses; this is not permission to redistribute every component. Fixture revisions require reviewing the upstream archive and expectations anew. There is no automatic golden update. This fixture covers one Fabric/Modrinth pack with required files and common overrides. The Quilt and NeoForge fixtures below add client-only declarations and an opaque local JAR. The legacy Forge fixture below adds omitted side defaults. The remaining real-pack corpus needs CurseForge, optional content, world templates, restricted files and custom-layer precedence. Synthetic fixtures and rolling surveys do not supply that evidence. Actual launcher import/startup remains a separate consumer obligation.

The direct-URL sentinel in `live_provider_cli` reuses the recorded `mods/morechathistory-1.3.1.jar` entry (3,573 bytes). It invokes ordinary `add` with the immutable CDN URL and checks the installed size/SHA-512 independently of empack's accepted-observation record. No extra upstream payload is committed. Changes to this metadata select both the direct-URL sentinel and the full pinned-import journey.

### Adrenaline 1.22.0 for Quilt

`adrenaline-1.22.0-quilt.json` pins Modrinth project `BYN9yKrV`, version `5rQpVqI5`, published as `1.22.0+1.20.1.quilt`. The 6,034-byte archive has SHA-256 `db5503b7ed011561ccccf6bb1a0d8b308cbe5f99f314ba26cf3feb8096943fe1`; its SHA-512 matches the pinned version record. Python's ZIP reader independently checked the archive CRCs and recorded the full index and override size/hash inventories. No upstream archive or mod file is committed.

The index selects Minecraft 1.20.1 and Quilt loader 0.26.0. All 17 files are required on the client; nine are unsupported on the server and eight are required on both sides. Their declared content totals 9,365,308 bytes. The archive also supplies ten common YOSBR configuration overrides. It has no optional file choices or auxiliary payload.

The shared journey checks those declarations in the retained lock and re-exported index, then verifies every acquired file and override in the bundled Prism client output. The expected launcher components are `net.minecraft` 1.20.1 and `org.quiltmc.quilt-loader` 0.26.0. A nested properties edit changes `useSmallThreadingDetector` from true to false, requires explicit adoption, and must appear in the next export without a version bump. These checks establish retained side authority and client inventory; they do not execute a server or establish Quilt startup/gameplay compatibility.

The upstream project's [license at a revision preceding this release](https://github.com/skywardmc/adrenaline/blob/4d53d763527c26dc15bd32e11c5493e41927246f/LICENSE) is MIT, copyright 2022 Ultra. Referenced mods keep their own licenses. Only metadata and the small configuration-value assertion are retained here; fixture changes require reviewing the exact archive, expectations and provenance again.

### Universalized Optimized 1.21.1 for NeoForge

`universalized-optimized-1.21.1-neoforge.json` records Modrinth project `Aa5L6RtV`, version `uQPo6CNj`, published as `1.21.1-NeoForge`. The pinned index names the pack Universalized Optimized 1.21.1; the catalog currently calls the project Simply Optimized Reloaded. The archive is 22,583 bytes with SHA-256 `b04844bab0010f1dae2a4b9d26cc1dd456e46b39d25a9a75d4053ff9ded02c2d`. Its SHA-512 matches the exact version record. Python's ZIP reader independently checked CRCs and the full index and override size/hash inventories.

The runtime is Minecraft 1.21.1 with NeoForge 21.1.194. All 13 referenced files are required on the client; five are unsupported on the server and eight are required on both sides. Referenced content totals 9,987,494 bytes. Fourteen common overrides total 23,292 bytes, including a 20,148-byte ThreadTweak JAR. The fixture has no optional choices, auxiliary payload or overlapping reference/override destinations.

The shared journey preserves the local JAR as opaque content alongside all exact references, verifies retained side authority, and checks complete Modrinth and bundled Prism client inventories. The expected launcher components are `net.minecraft` 1.21.1 and `net.neoforged` 21.1.194. Editing the imported FerriteCore properties requires explicit adoption and must update the export without changing the pack version or prior bundled artifact. No contained JAR, game or server is executed.

[Modrinth project metadata](https://api.modrinth.com/v2/project/Aa5L6RtV) reported MIT when this fixture was captured on 2026-11-01; this is a catalog observation, not an independently pinned upstream license file. Referenced and bundled mods retain their own licenses. Only expected metadata and the small properties assertion are committed, with no upstream archive or mod binary. Fixture updates require reviewing exact inputs and provenance; a moving catalog search cannot refresh the expectations automatically.

### Rapid Optimization for legacy Forge

`rapid-optimization-7.10an-2.1.1.json` pins Modrinth project `1q7QX7Ne`, version `8fbfT75J`, published as `7.10An.2.1.1`. Its 313,522-byte archive has SHA-256 `e6e07f7ed709aa5775c0f3f33dff8db33fd6f4eb2481412840a45a9e6f446484`, with SHA-512 matching the exact version record. Python's ZIP reader independently verified CRCs, the literal index and every override size/hash.

The runtime is Minecraft 1.7.10 with Forge 10.13.4.1614. Five references total 17,004,846 bytes. All omit the optional `env` object; the fixture checks retained required participation on both sides. The 31 common overrides total 399,779 bytes and include two local JARs, configuration, options and launcher-related assets. No optional choices or auxiliary top-level payloads are declared. Metadata is committed; the upstream archive and contained mods are not.

Raw source-index comparison stays exact before import. Export comparison only spells out a missing `env` object as required on both sides, preserving every explicit side setting and all other metadata. This reflects the [optional environment field](https://support.modrinth.com/en/articles/8802351-modrinth-modpack-format-mrpack) and the supported Prism source's [handling of an absent environment](https://github.com/PrismLauncher/PrismLauncher/blob/7d2d3c1ec6fcf8255ebacd02d9f792688575dfb4/launcher/modplatform/modrinth/ModrinthInstanceCreationTask.cpp#L407). A separate pure control protects that narrow comparison, including explicit values and a changed-digest negative case. It does not normalize receipts or validate otherwise malformed indexes.

The shared journey verifies full Modrinth and bundled Prism client inventories with `net.minecraft` 1.7.10 and `net.minecraftforge` 10.13.4.1614. A GTNHLib properties edit changes `enableFontRendererMixin` from true to false, retains the original surrounding bytes and line endings, and requires explicit adoption before rebuilding. It does not execute Java 8, a launcher or any contained mod.

[Modrinth project metadata](https://api.modrinth.com/v2/project/1q7QX7Ne) reported MIT when captured on 2026-11-01; no independently pinned upstream license file was located. Contained and referenced assets retain their own licenses. Fixture changes require reviewing exact inputs, expected semantics and provenance again.

### Horror OneBlock 1.1.1 with a saved world

`horror-oneblock-1.1.1-neoforge.json` pins Modrinth project `7y0dAVcr`, version `RgDwVwsB`, published as `Horror OneBlock 1.21.1-1.1.1`. The 221,749-byte archive has SHA-256 `1067624ed0d366167adc2a4d40b50452b7cb88e1b7177914f0b47714bfa67a6f`; its SHA-512 matches the exact catalog record. Python's ZIP reader independently checked CRCs, the complete index and every override size/hash without executing empack or any contained code.

The index selects Minecraft 1.21.1 and NeoForge 21.1.235. Its 44 references total 253,487,171 bytes, all declared required on both sides. The 100 common overrides total 1,804,117 bytes. Eleven are under `saves/Horror OneBlock/`: `level.dat`, an icon, entity and region files, and the world server-configuration readme. There are no optional or auxiliary entries. The shared scenario checks all source and acquired bytes through import, repeated sync, complete Modrinth and bundled Prism exports, and an explicitly adopted edit of that world readme. The expected launcher components are `net.minecraft` 1.21.1 and `net.neoforged` 21.1.235.

This fixture admits 96 MiB per bundled member and 256 MiB total decoded output, with the same 255-entry bound. Its largest declared reference is an 84,811,632-byte AmbientSounds JAR. The other four fixtures retain their original smaller bounds; acquisition and command deadlines are unchanged. Referenced mods are downloaded only by the selected live CI test, and neither they nor the saved world are committed. World bytes in a newly exported archive do not establish preservation of an already occupied player world, launcher startup or gameplay; those have separate acceptance checks.

[The catalog](https://api.modrinth.com/v2/project/7y0dAVcr) identifies the pack as all rights reserved, and no independently pinned license grant is claimed. The fixture records identities, sizes and digests rather than republishing the pack or its assets. Its referenced components retain their own licenses. Updating it requires reviewing the selected archive, expectations, provenance and admitted workload again.
